title: PulseScore: composite p50/p95 + network pulse scoring for region routing and tier-aware fallbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Implement a lightweight composite scoring system (PulseScore) that fuses latency percentiles (p50, p95) with short-term network pulse signals (packet loss rate, TCP retransmits, jitter, and path EWMA) to drive region selection and tier-aware fallback decisions. Motivation: current region chooser reacts too often to noisy p95 spikes and does not account for transient network blips; result is oscillation and poor tail-latency UX. PulseScore should be fast to compute, tunable per-customer/tier, and provide hysteresis/cooldown to prevent flip-flopping.

Key design elements:
- Inputs: p50, p95, recent packet_loss_pct (1m/5m), retransmit_rate, jitter_ms, path_stability_score (EWMA).
- Normalization: map each metric to a 0..1 degradation value using configurable percentiles/threshold curves and soft-clipping.
- Composite function: weighted sum with tunable weights: w_p50, w_p95, w_net. Default initial weights: 0.25, 0.55, 0.20.
- Trend-awareness: apply short-window EWMA on p95 and network pulse to favor persistent degradation vs single-sample spikes. EWMA half-life configurable per-tenant.
- Hysteresis & cooldown: require PulseScore delta > threshold for hold_duration before switching; enforce minimum hold window (e.g., 60s) and backoff multiplier for repeated switches.
- Tier biasing: integrate tenant tier multiplier so critical customers favor higher-tier regions unless PulseScore crosses a stricter threshold.
- Fallback variant selection: when region is degraded, router should prefer compatible model variants by quality-cost ladder; PulseScore maps to fallback severity bands (soft degrade -> quantized variant, hard degrade -> lower-cost variant + optional reduce-max-tokens).
- Safety override: global circuit-breaker to pause routing changes during infra incidents, controlled by ops.

Data & infra plan:
- Telemetry ingestion: extend region-telemetry stream to include retransmit_rate and jitter_ms in addition to existing percentiles; add 1m & 5m aggregates.
- Scoring service: new lightweight stateless scorer microservice that subscribes to telemetry and publishes per-region PulseScore to Redis KV with TTL. Scores are also sharded to reduce hot keys.
- Router integration: routing decision path queries scorer cache; fallback to last-good region if scorer missing. Add feature flag (pulse-routing) to gate rollout.
- Backfills / historical analysis: offline job to compute PulseScore on historical telemetry to tune thresholds per-region.
acceptance_criteria: PulseScore computed and persisted to cache for all regions with 1m and 5m cadence
Router reads PulseScore and adheres to hold_duration and hysteresis rules behind feature flag
Tier-aware thresholds applied and documented for at least three sample tenant tiers
Automated unit tests for score normalization and hysteresis logic, integration tests covering fallback variant selection
Staging canary shows reduced routing oscillation under synthetic spike tests (compare metric: switches/min reduced by >=50%)
Dashboards created (PulseScore per region, switch rate, candidate fallback counts) and alerts for high switch-rate and scoring gaps
